Commentary.Commentary: In the end, the trophy is handed to Harry Brook as England win this series 1-0. But, what a bummer, honestly, as we didn't get much cricket to see. Just one completed game sandwiched between two no results. But ultimately, weather is something, or the only thing, a human being cannot control. That's that from this three-match T20I series, then. Both teams will head to Mount Maunganui to kick off the 3 ODI series with the first match to be played at the iconic Bay Oval, before they head to Hamilton and Wellington for the rest of the two. The first ODI will be played on Sunday, 26th October, with the first ball scheduled to be bowled at 1 am GMT. Hope that rain stays away from that series. We sign off from here, but there is plenty of international cricket going on elsewhere. You can simply tab hop and follow the live action from those matches. Until next time, take care and cheers.

The captain of New Zealand, Mitchell Santner, is up for a chat. He starts by saying that this is a challenging time of year, but there were positives to take away. He adds that it is always nice to play against England. When asked about the positives, he highlights the way New Zealand bowled in the first game and notes that the second match was also a learning experience, as they were put under a lot of pressure on a good wicket. He mentions that the team started well in this match, and shares that they aimed to fine-tune their preparations ahead of the T20 World Cup. Admits that they won't get similar conditions in India or Sri Lanka, but stresses that the focus is to be prepared to play in different conditions.

The captain of England, Harry Brook, is also adjudged as the PLAYER OF THE SERIES. He says that it wasn't an ideal series but he is happy to win this. He adds that they are excited for the ODI series. He shares that they are having a good time in New Zealand and calls it a great place to play cricket, and they are looking forward to the ODI series. Says that they have a good balance in the side, with depth in the batting. Feels that they are in a really strong position. Speaking about the upcoming ODI series, he adds that there will be a few changes in the team, with some big names returning, and is hopeful that they can carry this momentum forward.
... THE PRESENTATION CEREMONY ...

Update - 9.15 am GMT - Here's the announcement. MATCH IS ABANDONED. The umpires have decided to pull the plug as the rain shows no sign of stopping. This hands England the series win in the three-match T20I contest by 1-0. Unfortunately, only one full game could be completed in what was a highly anticipated series. It is really frustrating, particularly for New Zealand, who had an opportunity to level the series, but only 3.4 overs were possible this evening due to unforgiving weather. Please stay tuned for the presentation which will be held indoors...

Update - 9.10 am GMT - Harry Brook is seen speaking with the umpires, likely trying to find out just how much longer the rain will continue before a decision is made. Meanwhile, rain has picked up and more covers are being unfurled. We don't have much left for the cut-off time, so the dreaded confirmation just might be around the corner.

Update - 9 am GMT - Booooooo... and just like that, the drizzle is back. Such a shame that we were just a couple of minutes away from the resumption, but the covers are back on. Some of the English players are tiptoeing the football in their dugout area, while the umpires have gathered on the sidelines for a detailed discussion, but going by their expressions, they are not pleased. Nobody seems particularly eager to get back on the field and the two stumps with microphones are being carried off as well. Guess that may be it.

Update - 8.51 am GMT - We have an update! According to the official word, the match is reduced to 8 overs a side. Batting Powerplay for the second innings will be of 2.2 overs, and 4 bowlers can bowl a maximum of 2 overs. So, Luke Wood's spell is done for the evening. Play resumes at 9 am GMT, which is in about 10 minutes or so.

Update - 8.47 am GMT - Quick update from Auckland is that the covers are coming off again. The stumps are being erected again and a rope is being dragged across the park as well. The umpires are out in the middle, with their umbrellas open. Optimistic to say that we will have a resumption time soon. Stay tuned.
Update - 8.36 am GMT - The groundsmen had started removing the covers, only for the rain to return, forcing them to put the covers back on. Ugh, this is frustrating!

Update - 8.20 am GMT - Good news! RAIN HAS STOPPED. Frankie Mackay reports from the ground, without an umbrella. But the concerning thing right now is the amount of water taken by the outfield. It was already greasy when the players came out after resumption. It will indeed take some time to dry the wet patches. Frankie also shares that the overhead conditions have settled down, with just an odd little spit around. Hopefully, this won't be a long delay. But for now, the pitch is under the covers. Stay tuned for further updates.
Update - 8.10 am GMT - And again! The rain is back, and so are the covers. Let's hope it goes away soon. Fingers crossed.

Commentary.Commentary: All set to resume at Eden Park. The umps and players walk out to the middle. English players spread to the field. Tim Robinson and Tim Seifert are ready to restart with the bat. Luke Wood to continue his over, which has three balls remaining. Here we go...

Update - 7.48 am GMT - We have an official update, folks! Play will resume at 7.50 am GMT, which is just a few minutes from now. And it will be a 14-over per side contest, and the Powerplay for both innings will be of 4.1 overs. The target for England will be adjusted through DLS.

Update - 7.45 am GMT - The umpires are out inspecting the playing area while England’s players warm up on the outfield. Conditions are looking promising for a fairly quick restart as long as the rain stays away.

Update - 7.38 am GMT - Some good news at last. An umpire inspection is scheduled in a few minutes. The ground staff are already hard at work, mopping up and trying to get the field ready for play. There is a rope being dragged across the field to dry up. Also, all covers are off. We are not far away from resuming soon.

Update - 7.31 am GMT - We have a very positive update from Auckland. Well, positive for now as it seems like the RAIN HAS STOPPED. The pitch is still under protection, but the bigger covers are being peeled off gradually. We might have a restart time and the revised playing conditions pretty soon through an official word. But surely, it will be a truncated game as it has been more than an hour and a half since the game halted. Stay tuned for the next update.

It’s a busy cricketing Thursday, and all eyes are on Navi Mumbai, where India Women and New Zealand Women are set to clash in one of the most crucial matches of the ICC Women’s Cricket World Cup 2025 at the DY Patil Stadium. With Australia, South Africa, and England already through to the knockouts, the fight is on for the final semifinal spot. India currently sit fourth on the points table, while New Zealand are right behind them in fifth. A win for the Kiwis would see them leapfrog India to fourth with six points, while a victory for India would keep them in their current position. However, a win for either side won’t confirm a semifinal berth yet, as both have a couple of games left. It’s a pressure cooker of a contest, and this one promises plenty of spice. That game will begin at 9.30 am GMT.

Rawalpindi has been breached, and how! South Africa storm back in style to boss the second Test, squaring the series 1-1 and dodging a series defeat against Pakistan. Their first win of the 2025-27 World Test Championship cycle, and they have made quite a statement with it. Meanwhile, there's more cricket coming your way, as in Dhaka, the third and final ODI is all set to get underway between Bangladesh and West Indies. Bangladesh won the toss and have elected to bat first. With the series leveled at 1-1, you can catch all the live action from that series decider by tab-hopping.

Update - 7.08 am GMT - It is still raining in Auckland. Not the heaviest of showers, but a rather consistent drizzle. The wait continues, and we are not far away from the overs getting trimmed as well. At the moment, prospects for a restart any time soon look bleak. All we can do is wait and hope. Stay tuned for further updates.

Over in Adelaide, India are batting first in the second ODI against Australia. Virat Kohli fell for a duck once more, marking the first time in his ODI career that he’s been dismissed without scoring in back-to-back innings. Rohit Sharma and Shreyas Iyer steadied the innings with a vital 118-run stand, both registering half-centuries. However, India lost momentum in the middle overs, collapsing from 135/2 to 174/5. Axar Patel once again played a valuable hand with a gritty 44, but with Australia striking at regular intervals, India look set for a below-par total. Hazlewood toiled hard, bowled his heart out, but without much luck, while Bartlett and Zampa have reaped the rewards, sharing maximum wickets amongst them. Last few overs remain in the first innings in that game, you can switch tabs and follow all the live action.

Meanwhile, South Africa are set to win the second Test match against Pakistan in Rawalpindi after losing the first. They only need 23 runs to win with all 10 wickets left. Spin bowlers Simon Harmer and Keshav Maharaj were the main wreckers for South Africa, taking a combined 17 wickets in the match. Harmer was especially crucial on the fourth morning, quickly dismissing key batters Babar Azam and Mohammad Rizwan. He also reached his 1000th first-class wicket during the innings.

Update - 6.30 am GMT - The pitch is already protected. But more covers are being brought to shield the squares as the rain seems to have picked up in intensity. It started with a frustrating mizzle, but it is coming heavier now. It could be a lengthy delay, we are afraid. It was supposed to come later in the evening, according to the weather reports, but you just cannot predict the weather in this part of the world. Stay tuned for further updates.
Update 6.18 am GMT - No, no, no! It has begun to drizzle here at Eden Park, and the umpires have called for covers. Let's hope it's just a passing shower.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the game to begin. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Tim Robinson and Tim Seifert walk in with their blades for New Zealand. Luke Wood has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

England's Luke Wood is in for a chat. He highlights that Phil Salt and Harry Brook look in some form. On being asked about bowling in the previous game, he shares that their plan was to bowl short and is glad that they did well to restrict New Zealand. He shares that Eden Park has some extra bounce and they will look to take advantage of these conditions by adjusting to the surface and executing their plans accordingly.

New Zealand's Matt Henry is up for a chat with Neil Wagner. Matt says that Eden Park is way different from Hagley Oval and they are prepared for it. Expects it to be fast and bouncy and states that the batters will have to adjust to the pace of the ball. He mentions that Eden Park offers steep bounce, but at this time of year, it’s crucial to make good use of the surface and strike early. He points out how England were clever in the second T20I, rotating the strike well with plenty of ones and twos. He stresses on the importance of breaking partnerships. Henry adds that the venue is always known for its swirling conditions and hopes there’s some moisture around to help with a bit of lateral movement.

The captain of New Zealand, Mitchell Santner, says that they bowled really well in the first game. Adds that it was a flat deck in the second game but the intent the guys showed was good. Ends by saying they will wait and see how the pitch plays.

The captain of England, Harry Brook, first highlights that the pitch in the second game was a belter to bat and they just tried to post a huge total on the board. Tells that this is a small ground with a bit of wind so they are happy to bowl. Mentions that best sides must do both but also adds that with the kind of batting depth they have, they back themselves to chase in this game.
England (Unchanged Playing XI) - Phil Salt, Jos Buttler (WK), Jacob Bethell, Harry Brook (C), Tom Banton, Sam Curran, Jordan Cox, Brydon Carse, Liam Dawson, Adil Rashid, and Luke Wood.

New Zealand (Playing XI) - Tim Seifert (WK), Tim Robinson, Rachin Ravindra, Mark Chapman, Daryl Mitchell, Michael Bracewell, James Neesham, Mitchell Santner (C), Zakary Foulkes (In for Kyle Jamieson), Matt Henry, and Jacob Duffy.
TOSS - The flip of the coin lands in favor of England and Harry Brook elects to BOWL first.

The weather in Auckland is not that pleasant. It is overcast and very windy at the moment. The forecast suggests there might be showers late in the evening. One game of this series has already ended in a no result. Let's hope we get a complete game of cricket.

Eden Park's smaller boundaries promise a high-scoring spectacle. Will England claim the series, or can New Zealand bounce back to level it? Tune in for what promises to be a fantastic finish to the three-match series. Toss and team news to follow shortly...

New Zealand's chase fell well short, getting bowled out for 171 despite a late flurry from captain Mitchell Santner. While Tim Seifert and Mark Chapman provided some stability, their strike rates weren't quick enough to keep up with the required run rate. The English bowling attack was superb, with the experienced Adil Rashid (4/32) leading the charge. The hosts need their top order to fire with much more intent in this do-or-die clash.

The visitors showed their class last time out, putting on a batting masterclass led by the explosive Phil Salt and skipper Harry Brook. Their massive 129-run partnership powered England to an imposing total of 236/4. The Kiwis will need a much sharper bowling performance to contain this powerful English lineup, as their bowlers struggled to find any economy at Hagley Oval.

Welcome to the series decider! The stage is set for a thrilling final T20I between New Zealand and England at the iconic Eden Park in Auckland. England, led by Harry Brook, holds the advantage with an unassailable 1-0 lead after their dominant victory in the second T20I in Christchurch. They can't lose the series, but a win here is essential to seal it outright. New Zealand, however, has everything to play for. To avoid consecutive series defeats, the Blackcaps must secure a victory on their home turf.
... MATCH DAY ...

The scene shifts to Auckland for the final and deciding match of this series, where the stakes couldn't be higher. After the first game was effectively lost to the weather, England seized a massive advantage, posting a huge total of 236/4 and securing a comfortable 65-run win. That commanding performance means the tourists are now just one victory away from sealing the series. For New Zealand, however, it's simple. They must win this fixture and level the series at 1-1 and avoid a defeat on home soil. This final showdown at a ground known for its short boundaries promises a dramatic, high-octane conclusion. The key area for New Zealand to address is undoubtedly their bowling, which proved far too expensive in the last outing, leaking runs at a rate over 10 an over. Captain Mitchell Santner needs his attack, including main pacers like Matt Henry, to find a better line and length right from the first ball. They need to 'keep a lid on things' early, giving their batters a realistic target to chase. On the batting front, the home side will be looking for a big effort from key players like Tim Seifert, Mark Chapman, and Daryl Mitchell. These hitters must come to the party and stay on the 'front foot' to take the game to the English attack if they are to successfully chase a daunting total. England, meanwhile, are riding a wave of confidence, particularly with the bat. Phil Salt and skipper Harry Brook led the charge beautifully, backed up by a fantastic little cameo from Tom Banton, showing the incredible depth of their batting line-up. Their bowlers were then able to 'relish the cushion' of the huge total, with Luke Wood, Brydon Carse, Adil Rashid, and Liam Dawson all chipping in with crucial wickets and proving very effective. Sam Curran, though wicketless, continues to impress with his all-round game. They will be aiming to hit the opposition hard and early, driving home their advantage' to lift the series trophy in Auckland.
